topic: Light pollution hides the Milky Way
script: More than a third of people on Earth cannot see the Milky Way from home. Artificial light at night brightens the sky and drowns out faint stars. In a 2016 study, about 80 percent of North Americans could not see it. Under truly dark skies, you can see a few thousand stars with your eyes. From a bright city, you may see only a few dozen. Shielding outdoor lights so they point down helps bring the stars back. Follow WonderBytes for more facts that sound fake but are true.
